steps.label: Do Now: Question 1
steps.content:
Do Now: Follow It, Then Correct It

Think → Pair → ShareWhy must you follow what each line says, and not what the program should do?Show the answer

The computer only does what the lines say. You can only see an error if you trace what really happens.

4 minutes. What to do: from 3.1. The program should add up 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6. First follow it exactly as it is written. Stuck? Press Walk me through it. Done when Check answers gives 3 marks.

01  DECLARE Total : INTEGER
02  DECLARE Count : INTEGER
03  Total ← 0
04  FOR Count ← 1 TO 6
05      Total ← Total + 2
06  NEXT Count
07  OUTPUT Total
Total: 3 marks

walkthrough.title: Walk me through it: follow it, then find the error

steps.text: This is a different program. It should add up 2, 3 and 4. Follow what each line says, not what it should do.
steps.visual:
01  DECLARE Sum : INTEGER
02  DECLARE Num : INTEGER
03  Sum ← 0
04  FOR Num ← 2 TO 4
05      Sum ← Sum + 10
06  NEXT Num
07  OUTPUT Sum

steps.text: Sum is set to 0 once, before the loop.
steps.visual:
01  DECLARE Sum : INTEGER
02  DECLARE Num : INTEGER
03  Sum ← 0
04  FOR Num ← 2 TO 4
05      Sum ← Sum + 10
06  NEXT Num
07  OUTPUT Sum
Sum = 0

steps.text: The loop runs with Num = 2, then Num = 3, then Num = 4. On each pass the line inside the loop adds 10. It never uses Num.
steps.visual:
01  DECLARE Sum : INTEGER
02  DECLARE Num : INTEGER
03  Sum ← 0
04  FOR Num ← 2 TO 4
05      Sum ← Sum + 10
06  NEXT Num
07  OUTPUT Sum
Sum = 10, then 20, then 30

steps.text: As written, it outputs 30. It should output 2 + 3 + 4 = 9. The value first goes wrong on the line inside the loop.
steps.visual:
01  DECLARE Sum : INTEGER
02  DECLARE Num : INTEGER
03  Sum ← 0
04  FOR Num ← 2 TO 4
05      Sum ← Sum + 10
06  NEXT Num
07  OUTPUT Sum
Output as written: 30

steps.text: The fix: that line must add the loop variable, not a fixed number. Trace again to prove it gives 9. Now do the same steps with your program.
steps.visual:
01  DECLARE Sum : INTEGER
02  DECLARE Num : INTEGER
03  Sum ← 0
04  FOR Num ← 2 TO 4
05      Sum ← Sum + 10
06  NEXT Num
07  OUTPUT Sum

steps.label: Do Now: Question 2
steps.content:
Do Now: A Loop with an IF

Think → Pair → ShareWhy do you check the IF line again on every pass of the loop?Show the answer

The loop variable changes on every pass, so the condition can be TRUE on one pass and FALSE on the next.

4 minutes. What to do: from 3.2. Trace the loop. Check the IF line on every pass. Stuck? Press Walk me through it. Done when Check answers gives 3 marks.

01  DECLARE Count : INTEGER
02  DECLARE Total : INTEGER
03  Total ← 0
04  FOR Count ← 2 TO 8
05      IF Count >= 6 THEN
06          Total ← Total + Count
07      ENDIF
08  NEXT Count
09  OUTPUT Total
Total: 3 marks

walkthrough.title: Walk me through it: a loop with an IF

steps.text: This is a different program. Num goes from 1 to 5. Check the IF line on every pass.
steps.visual:
01  DECLARE Num : INTEGER
02  DECLARE Sum : INTEGER
03  Sum ← 0
04  FOR Num ← 1 TO 5
05      IF Num >= 4 THEN
06          Sum ← Sum + Num
07      ENDIF
08  NEXT Num
09  OUTPUT Sum
Sum = 0

steps.text: While Num is less than 4, Num >= 4 is FALSE. The line inside the IF does not run, so Sum stays 0.
steps.visual:
01  DECLARE Num : INTEGER
02  DECLARE Sum : INTEGER
03  Sum ← 0
04  FOR Num ← 1 TO 5
05      IF Num >= 4 THEN
06          Sum ← Sum + Num
07      ENDIF
08  NEXT Num
09  OUTPUT Sum
Sum = 0

steps.text: Num = 4: 4 >= 4 is TRUE, because 4 is equal to 4. Sum = 0 + 4 = 4. Num = 5: TRUE again. Sum = 4 + 5 = 9.
steps.visual:
01  DECLARE Num : INTEGER
02  DECLARE Sum : INTEGER
03  Sum ← 0
04  FOR Num ← 1 TO 5
05      IF Num >= 4 THEN
06          Sum ← Sum + Num
07      ENDIF
08  NEXT Num
09  OUTPUT Sum
The IF was TRUE 2 times. Sum = 9

steps.text: The loop ends, and the last line outputs Sum.
steps.visual:
01  DECLARE Num : INTEGER
02  DECLARE Sum : INTEGER
03  Sum ← 0
04  FOR Num ← 1 TO 5
05      IF Num >= 4 THEN
06          Sum ← Sum + Num
07      ENDIF
08  NEXT Num
09  OUTPUT Sum
Output: 9

steps.text: With > 4, the pass with Num = 4 is FALSE: 4 is not more than 4. Only 5 is added, so it outputs 5. Now trace your program the same way.
steps.visual:
01  DECLARE Num : INTEGER
02  DECLARE Sum : INTEGER
03  Sum ← 0
04  FOR Num ← 1 TO 5
05      IF Num > 4 THEN
06          Sum ← Sum + Num
07      ENDIF
08  NEXT Num
09  OUTPUT Sum
Output: 5

steps.label: 3.R: Pseudocode and Loops Review
steps.content:
Pseudocode and Software Development

Pseudocode and Loops Review

Year 9, 3.R

Think → Pair → ShareWhy is it useful to review two lessons before you learn something new?Show the answer

New work builds on old work. A gap you fix now will not stop you later.

  • 1 minute. What to do: read this slide, then press Next.
  • Today you work on your own. The slides teach you. Read each slide, answer it, then press Next.
  • Part 1: 3.1 Following and Correcting Pseudocode, then Data Bridge 3D. Part 2: 3.2 Algorithms with Loops, then Data Bridge 3D. Then more Data Bridge 3D.
  • Stuck in Data Bridge 3D? On the start screen press Start Learn mode. It shows a worked example and gives free help. It does not count, so go back to Play when you can.
  • Notes: press the pen icon at the top. Write down every mistake and the reason.

steps.label: 3.1: One Line at a Time
steps.content:
3.1: One Line at a Time

Think → Pair → ShareWhy does a line change only the variable on the left of the arrow?Show the answer

The arrow means: work out the right side, then store the result in the variable on the left. No other variable is touched.

1 minute. What to do: follow the program one line at a time, then choose. Done when you have read the reason.

01  DECLARE A : INTEGER
02  DECLARE B : INTEGER
03  A ← 6
04  B ← A
05  A ← A + 3
06  OUTPUT B

One line at a time, from the top.
A line changes only the variable on the left of the arrow.

items.explain: Line 4 copies 6 into B. Line 5 changes only A, so B is still 6.

steps.label: 3.1: Inside or After the Loop?
steps.content:
3.1: Inside or After the Loop?

Think → Pair → ShareWhy can moving just one line change what a program does?Show the answer

The computer follows the lines in order. A line in a new place runs at a different time, or a different number of times.

2 minutes. What to do: only one line has moved. Predict, then read the reason. Done when you can say what A and B output.

Program A

01  DECLARE Number : INTEGER
02  DECLARE Count : INTEGER
03  Number ← 2
04  FOR Count ← 1 TO 3
05      Number ← Number * 3
06      OUTPUT Number
07  NEXT Count

Program B

01  DECLARE Number : INTEGER
02  DECLARE Count : INTEGER
03  Number ← 2
04  FOR Count ← 1 TO 3
05      Number ← Number * 3
06  NEXT Count
07  OUTPUT Number

items.prompt: Predict: how many numbers does program A output?
items.explain: In A, OUTPUT is inside the loop, so it runs on every pass: 6, 18, 54. In B, it is after NEXT, so it runs once: 54.

steps.label: 3.1: The Value on the Line
steps.content:
3.1: The Value on the Line

Think → Pair → ShareWhy test the value exactly on the line, and not only values far from it?Show the answer

Values far from the line give the same result in both programs. Only the value on the line shows the difference.

2 minutes. What to do: predict, then read the reason. Done when you can say why A and B are different.

Program A

01  DECLARE Age : INTEGER
02  INPUT Age
03  IF Age > 13 THEN
04      OUTPUT "Join"
05  ELSE
06      OUTPUT "Too young"
07  ENDIF

Program B

01  DECLARE Age : INTEGER
02  INPUT Age
03  IF Age >= 13 THEN
04      OUTPUT "Join"
05  ELSE
06      OUTPUT "Too young"
07  ENDIF

items.prompt: Predict: the user types 13. What does program A output?
items.explain: 13 > 13 is FALSE: 13 is not more than 13, so A outputs Too young. In B, 13 >= 13 is TRUE, so B outputs Join.

steps.label: 3.1: Four Steps to Correct a Program
steps.content:
3.1: Four Steps to Correct a Program

Think → Pair → ShareWhy must you know the purpose of a program before you can correct it?Show the answer

An error is a difference between what a program does and what it should do. Without the purpose there is nothing to compare with.

2 minutes. What to do: purpose: input three prices and output their total. The user types 7, 5, 9. It outputs 9, not 21. Use the four steps, then choose. Done when you have read the reason.

01  DECLARE Price : INTEGER
02  DECLARE Count : INTEGER
03  DECLARE Total : INTEGER
04  Total ← 0
05  FOR Count ← 1 TO 3
06      INPUT Price
07      Total ← Price
08  NEXT Count
09  OUTPUT Total

1 Purpose: what should it output?
2 Trace: follow it exactly as written.
3 Find: the first line that makes a value go wrong.
4 Fix and prove: change that line, then trace again.

items.prompt: Which line causes the wrong result?
items.explain: Line 7 stores only the new Price, so the old total is lost. Line 9 only shows it. Fix: Total ← Total + Price. A new trace outputs 21.

steps.label: Data Bridge 3D: Following and Correcting Pseudocode
steps.content:
Data Bridge 3D: Following and Correcting Pseudocode

Think → Pair → ShareWhy trace a program on paper before you type your answer?Show the answer

Each step on paper can be checked. A step done only in your head is easy to get wrong.

12 minutes. What to do: Answer the question in the side panel to earn coins. W A S D walk, B build, E use, in the cart hold Space on RED. Stuck? Start Learn mode. Done when you cross 2 gaps in Play. At 13:48, press Next.

steps.label: 3.2: A Loop in a Flowchart
steps.content:
3.2: A Loop in a Flowchart

Think → Pair → ShareWhy does the arrow go back to the decision, and not back to Start?Show the answer

Going back to Start would set the values back to their start values. The decision checks whether to run the boxes one more time.

2 minutes. What to do: follow the flowchart. Say the value of Count and Total each time you reach the decision. Then choose. Done when you have read the reason.

The arrow back up to the decision makes the loop.
Yes: run the boxes again. No: leave the loop.

items.explain: Yes for Count = 1, 2 and 3: three passes, adding 4 each time. Then 4 <= 3 is No, so it outputs 12.

steps.label: 3.2: Flowchart and FOR Loop
steps.content:
3.2: Flowchart and FOR Loop

Think → Pair → ShareWhy can one FOR line replace three boxes in a flowchart?Show the answer

A FOR loop does the three jobs for you: it sets the start value, checks the last value, and adds 1 at NEXT.

2 minutes. What to do: use the table to match a flowchart to a FOR loop, then choose. Done when you have read the reason.

FlowchartFOR loop
Count ← 1FOR Count ← 1 ...
Count <= 3?... TO 3
Count ← Count + 1NEXT Count
Total ← Total + CountTotal ← Total + Count

Same steps, same values, same output.

items.prompt: A flowchart sets Count ← 3, asks Count <= 7? and adds 1 each pass. Which FOR line matches?
items.explain: 7 <= 7 is TRUE, so the last pass is 7: 3 TO 7. 3 TO 8 runs once too many.

steps.label: 3.2: One Row Each Pass
steps.content:
3.2: One Row Each Pass

Think → Pair → ShareWhy use the value in the row above, and not the start value?Show the answer

Each pass changes Score, so the next pass starts from the new value.

3 minutes. What to do: finish the trace table in your head or on paper. Write a new row each time a value changes. Use the value in the row above. Done when Check answers gives 2 marks.

01  DECLARE Score : INTEGER
02  DECLARE Count : INTEGER
03  Score ← 30
04  FOR Count ← 1 TO 4
05      Score ← Score - Count
06  NEXT Count
07  OUTPUT Score
CountScoreOutput
30
129
227
3?
4??
Total: 2 marks

Think → Pair → ShareWhy write a trace table for a loop, even for a short one?Show the answer

Every pass changes the values. A table keeps each value in its own row, so none is lost or mixed up.
